report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**. The Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing) intrauterine system is officially FDA-approved to prevent pregnancy for up to **five years**.

### Evidence & Context

* **FDA Prescribing Information:** Official labeling from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration states that Kyleena (containing 19.5 mg levonorgestrel) is indicated for pregnancy prevention for up to five years, after which it must be removed or replaced.
* **Source of Common Misconceptions:** Scepticism about this timeframe often stems from confusion with other intrauterine devices (IUDs):
  * Higher-dose progestin IUDs (such as Mirena and Liletta) have had their FDA approvals extended from 5 years up to **8 years** based on extended clinical trials.
  * Non-hormonal copper IUDs (such as Paragard) are approved for up to **10 years**.
* **No Extended-Use Approval:** Clinical guidelines note that lower-dose systems like Kyleena (5 years) and Skyla (3 years) have not been approved for off-label extended use past their designated timelines. Consequently, Kyleena must be replaced at the 5-year mark to maintain reliable contraceptive protection.

### Sources
* **FDA Prescribing Information (Kyleena):** https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/208224s005lbl.pdf
* **DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine):** https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080
* **Planned Parenthood - IUD Information:** https://www.plannedparenthood.org/learn/birth-control/iud
* **NASPAG - LARC Extended Use Talking Points:** https://www.naspag.org/assets/docs/LARC+extended+use+talking+points.pdf
